# Setup
```{r, echo=TRUE}
set.seed(12242987)
library(knitr)
library(DPpackage)
```

# Simulate data
```{r, echo=TRUE}
n <- 500
x <- runif(n, 0, 1)
y <- sapply(x, function(xi) {
  if (runif(1) < exp(-2 * xi)) {
    rnorm(1, mean = 0, sd = 0.1)
  } else {
    rnorm(1, mean = xi^2, sd = 0.2)
  }
})
data <- data.frame(x = x, y = y)
kable(head(data), caption = "Generated data")
```

# Fit the DPdensity model

```{r, echo=TRUE}
# Define hyperparameters
prior <- list(
  a0 = 10,
  b0 = 1,
  nu1 = 4,
  nu2 = 4,
  m2 = c(0, 0), # mean vector for the prior distribution
  s2 = diag(2), # covariance matrix for the prior
  psiinv2 = solve(diag(2)), # inverse covariance matrix
  tau1 = 6.01,
  tau2 = 3.01
)

# MCMC parameters
mcmc <- list(
  nburn = 5000, # burn-in period
  nsave = 5000, # number of samples to save
  nskip = 4, # thinning interval
  ndisplay = 100 # display every 100 iterations
)
fit <- DPdensity(
  y = y,
  prior = prior,
  mcmc = mcmc,
  state = NULL,
  status = TRUE
)
```

# Plot results
```{r, echo=TRUE}
y_grid <- seq(min(y), max(y), length.out = 100) # grid for evaluating densities

# compute conditional densities
x_values <- c(0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75) # values of x to evaluate
density_results <- lapply(x_values, function(x_val) {
  # weights
  weights <- exp(-2 * x_val)

  # component densities
  y1_density <- dnorm(y_grid, mean = 0, sd = 0.1) # Component 1
  y2_density <- dnorm(y_grid, mean = x_val^2, sd = 0.2) # Component 2

  # combined density
  conditional_density <- weights * y1_density + (1 - weights) * y2_density

  list(grid = y_grid, density = conditional_density)
})

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
for (i in seq_along(x_values)) {
  plot(
    density_results[[i]]$grid, density_results[[i]]$density,
    type = "l", col = "blue", lwd = 2,
    xlab = "y", ylab = "Density",
    main = paste("Density at x =", x_values[i])
  )
}
```

The plots show the transition of the conditional density.
We can see that for x = 0.1 and 0.25 the density is unimodal but for 0.5 and 0.75 it becomes
bimodal where for x = 0.75 it becomes more pronounced
